# Specs generated from the Lean model

Each folder is a requirement spec with one `requirements.md`, generated from the rules in one Lean module. The acceptance criteria are in EARS notation, and the folders follow the layout Kiro reads. The rule's docstring holds the user story and the acceptance criteria; the build computes each criterion's status from the theorems and examples tagged `@[checks]` with its ID. To change a requirement, edit the docstring and rebuild.

35 acceptance criteria: 21 proven, 0 example only, 14 open, 0 not checked.

9 rules: 0 confirmed, 0 confirmed but out of date, 9 written from a source, 0 assumed by the modeller.

| [The photoid credential](one-id-the-photoid-credential/requirements.md) | OID-102 | As an issuer, I want to know which recommendations of the guide a photoid I issue does not follow, so that I can decide whether to add the passport data a border authority may ask for later. | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

| [The boarding pass credential](one-id-the-boarding-pass-credential/requirements.md) | OID-103 | As an airport touchpoint, I want every boarding pass credential I accept to carry one boarding pass string in the standard format, so that I can process it as I process a printed or mobile bar code. | 6 | 5 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| [How long a credential stays valid](one-id-how-long-a-credential-stays-valid/requirements.md) | OID-104 | As an airline, I want a boarding pass credential to stop being valid shortly after the journey's last flight leaves, so that it cannot be presented again once the journey is over. | 5 | 3 | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| [How long a credential stays valid](one-id-how-long-a-credential-stays-valid/requirements.md) | OID-105 | As a relying party, I want a credential to count as expired once its validity has ended, so that I never act on a boarding pass or a photoid that is no longer in force. | 4 | 3 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| [How long a credential stays valid](one-id-how-long-a-credential-stays-valid/requirements.md) | OID-108 | As a border authority, I want a photoid to stop being valid when the passport it was derived from expires, so that an expired passport is not accepted in digital form. | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| [Credentials and their data elements](one-id-credentials-and-their-data-elements/requirements.md) | OID-106 | As a relying party, I want to name one data element of a credential by its namespace and its identifier, so that I can request only that element and the wallet can disclose it without the others. | 3 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 0 |

## Acceptance criteria

| ID | Criterion | Status | Checked by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OID-101.1 | IF the document type of a credential is not the photoid document type THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it as a photoid. | proven | proven theorem `not_photoid_and_boardingPass`; proven theorem `photoid_docType`; example `documentTypes` |
| OID-101.2 | IF a photoid lacks the base identity namespace THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | proven | proven theorem `photoid_has_base` |
| OID-101.3 | IF a photoid lacks a data element that Table C.1 marks mandatory in the base identity namespace THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | proven | proven theorem `photoid_has_mandatory_base` |
| OID-101.4 | IF a data element of the base identity namespace does not have the encoding Table C.1 gives it THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the photoid. | proven | proven theorem `photoid_base_encoding`; example `portraitInTheWrongEncoding` |
| OID-101.5 | IF a photoid has no portrait THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | open | open theorem `photoid_has_portrait`; counterexample `photoidWithoutPortrait` |
| OID-101.6 | IF a photoid carries a namespace other than the three the guide lists, or a data element its table does not list THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | open | open theorem `photoid_only_listed`; counterexample `photoidWithUnlistedData` |
| OID-101.7 | IF a photoid carries a portrait and a data group 2 that differ THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | open | open theorem `portrait_is_dg2`; counterexample `portraitDiffersFromDataGroup` |
| OID-101.8 | IF a photoid carries the photoid namespace without a data element that Table C.2 marks mandatory THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | open | open theorem `photoid_nameSpace_complete`; counterexample `photoidNameSpaceIncomplete` |
| OID-101.9 | IF a photoid carries the data groups namespace without a data element that Table C.3 marks mandatory THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | open | open theorem `dataGroups_nameSpace_complete`; counterexample `dataGroupsNameSpaceIncomplete` |
| OID-102.1 | WHEN a photoid lacks the photoid namespace or the data groups namespace THE SYSTEM SHALL report each missing namespace as a recommendation it does not follow. | proven | proven theorem `advises_dataGroups_nameSpace`; proven theorem `advises_photoid_nameSpace`; example `minimalPhotoid` |
| OID-102.2 | WHEN a photoid carries the photoid namespace without the image captured at enrolment THE SYSTEM SHALL report the missing image as a recommendation it does not follow. | proven | proven theorem `advises_enrolment_portrait` |
| OID-102.3 | WHEN a photoid was derived from a document other than a passport THE SYSTEM SHALL report that as a recommendation it does not follow. | proven | proven theorem `advises_source_document`; example `photoidFromAnIdentityCard` |
| OID-102.4 | WHEN a photoid lacks the photoid namespace or the data groups namespace THE SYSTEM SHALL report no broken requirement for the missing namespace. | proven | proven theorem `recommended_nameSpace_never_required`; example `minimalPhotoid` |
| OID-109.1 | IF a photoid was derived from a document other than a passport THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | open | open theorem `photoid_from_passport`; counterexample `photoidFromAnIdentityCard` |
| OID-103.1 | IF the document type of a credential is not the boarding pass document type THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it as a boarding pass. | proven | proven theorem `boardingPass_docType`; proven theorem `not_photoid_and_boardingPass`; example `documentTypes` |
| OID-103.2 | IF a boarding pass lacks the boarding pass namespace THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | proven | proven theorem `boardingPass_has_string`; example `boardingPassStrings` |
| OID-103.3 | IF a boarding pass lacks the boarding pass string THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | proven | proven theorem `boardingPass_has_string`; example `boardingPassStrings` |
| OID-103.4 | IF the boarding pass string is not a text string THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the boarding pass. | proven | proven theorem `boardingPass_has_string`; proven theorem `boardingPass_strings_follow`; example `boardingPassStrings` |
| OID-103.5 | IF the boarding pass string does not follow IATA Resolution 792 THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the boarding pass. | proven | proven theorem `boardingPass_has_string`; proven theorem `boardingPass_strings_follow`; example `boardingPassStrings` |
| OID-103.6 | IF a boarding pass carries a namespace or a data element the guide does not list THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | open | open theorem `boardingPass_only_listed`; counterexample `boardingPassWithExtraNameSpace` |
| OID-104.1 | IF the validity of a boarding pass ends before the departure of the last leg of its journey THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | proven | proven theorem `validity_reaches_departure` |
| OID-104.2 | IF the validity of a boarding pass ends later than soon after the departure of the last leg of its journey THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | proven | proven theorem `validity_ends_soon_after` |
| OID-104.3 | WHILE the current time is before the departure of the last leg of the journey THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the boarding pass as not expired. | proven | proven theorem `valid_before_departure` |
| OID-104.4 | WHEN the journey is completed THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the boarding pass as expired. | open | open theorem `expired_once_journey_completed`; counterexample `validAfterTheJourney` |
| OID-104.5 | WHILE the last leg of the journey has not actually departed THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the boarding pass as not expired. | open | open theorem `valid_until_actual_departure`; counterexample `expiredBeforeADelayedDeparture` |
| OID-105.1 | WHEN the current time is after the end of a credential's validity THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the credential as expired. | proven | proven theorem `expired_after_validUntil` |
| OID-105.2 | WHILE the current time is before the end of a credential's validity THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the credential as not expired. | proven | proven theorem `valid_before_validUntil` |
| OID-105.3 | WHEN a credential has expired THE SYSTEM SHALL treat it as expired at every later time. | proven | proven theorem `expired_stays_expired` |
| OID-105.4 | WHILE the current time is no later than the end of a credential's validity THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the credential as not expired. | open | open theorem `valid_at_validUntil`; counterexample `atTheEndOfValidity` |
| OID-108.1 | WHEN the document a photoid was derived from has expired THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the photoid as expired. | open | open theorem `photoid_expires_with_document`; counterexample `photoidOutlivesItsPassport` |
| OID-106.1 | WHEN the namespace names of a credential and the identifiers within each namespace are unique THE SYSTEM SHALL return the value of each data element for the name of its namespace and its identifier. | proven | proven theorem `element_addressable` |
| OID-106.2 | IF a credential has no data element with a given namespace name and identifier THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return no value for them. | proven | proven theorem `element_absent` |
| OID-106.3 | IF two namespaces of a credential have the same name, or two data elements of one namespace have the same identifier THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the credential. | open | open theorem `boardingPass_names_unique`; open theorem `photoid_names_unique`; counterexample `repeatedIdentifier`; counterexample `twoBoardingPassStrings` |
| OID-107.1 | IF a photoid and a boarding pass presented together are about different travelers THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the pair. | open | open theorem `matched_pair_same_traveler`; counterexample `anotherTravelersBoardingPass`; counterexample `twoTravelersWithOneName` |
| OID-107.2 | WHEN a photoid and a boarding pass presented together are about the same traveler THE SYSTEM SHALL accept the pair. | open | open theorem `same_traveler_matches`; counterexample `ownBoardingPassRefused` |

The build writes the same rows to `build/ears-criteria.csv`, one row per rule to `build/ears.csv`, each rule's sources and confirmation to `build/provenance.csv`, and the assumptions about external specifications to `build/assumptions.csv`. The site serves all four at its root.
